<nav aria-label="Documentation">

    <Menu.Section label="Components" defaultOpen>

accessibility:
- The root `Menu` renders as `<aside class="menu">`. A menu that's navigation is better inside a
  `<nav>` with an `aria-label`, which gives assistive tech a navigation landmark to jump to.
- Every `Menu.List` has `role="list"`, nested ones included. That's the role a `<ul>` already has,
  set again for Safari, whose WebKit stops exposing a `<ul>` as a list once its markers are hidden,
  as Bulma's reset hides them, unless the role is written out.
- `Menu.Item active` sets `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, the link by
  default, so the current item isn't only a color. An `aria-current` you pass wins: a menu of
  sections on one page can say `"location"`, and `aria-current={false}` turns it off.
- Use semantic nesting (`Menu.List` inside `Menu.Item`) for submenus.
- Give each item an `href`, a router link through `as`, or `as="button"`, so the keyboard can
  reach it.
- `Menu.Item as="button"` defaults to `type="button"`, so a menu item inside a form doesn't
  submit it. Pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"` and yours is used instead; any other value
  renders `type="button"`.
- In forced colors (Windows' contrast themes), the browser replaces Bulma's fill and text color
  for the active item along with every other color, so bestax's stylesheet marks an
  `is-active` or `is-selected` item with a bar in the system's highlight color along its start
  edge there instead. The item's text, and an icon or a tag inside it, keep the colors your
  contrast theme gives them. That rule ships in `bestax.css` and `extras.css`, not in Bulma's
  own stylesheet.

For `Menu.Section`, a section that opens and closes:

- It follows APG's
  [Disclosure Navigation Menu example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/).
  The heading is a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` naming the
  wrapper around its list. Enter and Space open and close it, as they do any button, and it
  doesn't submit a form it sits in.
- The links under it are ordinary links. Each is its own tab stop, and there's no roving focus or
  arrow-key handling, which is a tree's model rather than navigation's. They keep their `href`,
  so a link still opens in a new tab, and `active` still sets `aria-current="page"`.
- A closed section's list is `hidden` and `inert`, so it isn't drawn, Tab skips its links, and
  assistive tech and find-in-page don't reach them. `inert` keeps the links out of reach even if a
  stylesheet sets `display` on the list and shows it. The list stays in the page, so
  `aria-controls` always names an element that exists, and a section that starts closed is
  already closed in the server's HTML, before any script runs.
- Open the section that holds the current page, with `defaultOpen` or `open`, so the link marked
  `aria-current` can be seen and reached.
- When the app closes a section while focus is on one of its links, as a sidebar that keeps only
  the current route's section open does after a link is followed, focus moves to that section's
  heading. Without that, the browser drops focus to the page, and the next Tab starts from the
  top.
- `label` is the button's content and its accessible name. Keep links and other buttons out of
  it.
- In forced colors the chevron stays visible, since it's drawn as a border, and the focus ring
  takes the system's text color. In a right-to-left page the chevron sits at the left end of the
  heading and points left while closed. It turns with a short transition, which stops when the
  reader asks for reduced motion.

:::note
For router integrations, pass the correct `as` and `to`/`href` props to `Menu.Item`.
:::
summary: The `Menu` component provides Bulma's vertical navigation menu: a simple, accessible sidebar or section menu for your Bulma React UI.

parts.summary: The `Menu` component provides Bulma's vertical navigation menu: a simple, accessible sidebar or section menu for your Bulma React UI.
parts.catchAll: All standard HTML attributes and Bulma helper props

All standard

attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: MenuList applies `menu-list` class only at the top level (not for nested lists). Every level renders `role="list"`, which Safari needs: WebKit stops exposing a `<ul>` as a list once its markers are hidden, and Bulma's reset hides them.

extraProps.name: role
extraProps.description: Ignored: every level renders `role="list"` in its place, so a menu or tree role can't go here.

parts.catchAll: All standard <ul> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: MenuItem supports `as` prop for custom link components, e.g., react-router-dom Link. Give each item an `href`, a router link through `as`, or `as="button"`, so the keyboard can reach it: an `<a>` with no `href` isn't a link, and Tab skips it.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom link component (e.g. `Link` from router). `'button'` renders `type="button"` unless you pass `type="submit"` or `type="reset"`, so an item inside a form does not submit it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the wrapping `<li>`.

props.name: children
props.description: Item content and optional nested MenuList.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks the item as the current one. It adds Bulma's `is-active` class, and `aria-current="page"` on the element `as` renders, so assistive tech can tell which item is current too. An `aria-current` you pass wins, even `undefined`: use it to say something else (`"location"` for a section of one page, say), or `aria-current={false}` to turn it off. A menu should mark one page, so when the section above the current page is `active` too, give it `aria-current="location"`, and give an `active` item that isn't navigation, such as an `as="button"` filter, `aria-current={false}`.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the inner element `as` renders, not the wrapping `<li>`, typed from `as`: the DOM node for an intrinsic tag, or whatever handle a custom component exposes.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element or component selected by as (default <a>) and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: A section of the menu that opens and closes: its heading is a button drawn like `Menu.Label`, and its `Menu.List` of links shows while it's open. It's APG's disclosure navigation, for a sidebar of link groups: the links stay ordinary links, each its own tab stop, and a closed section's list is `hidden` and `inert`, so Tab and assistive tech skip it. It goes directly in `Menu`, holding a `Menu.List`. Closing it while focus is on one of its links moves focus to its heading.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the wrapping `<div>`.

props.name: label
props.description: **Required.** The section's heading, drawn like `Menu.Label` inside the button that opens and closes it. Keep links and buttons out of it, since it's inside one.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Menu.List` of links the section shows while it's open. The section itself goes directly in `Menu`, beside its labels and lists: inside a `Menu.Item` it would render inside the item's link, and inside a `Menu.List` it wouldn't be a list item.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. If provided, the section is controlled, and its button only reports through `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state for uncontrolled usage. Open the section that holds the current page, so the reader sees where they are.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the state the button asks for (`true` to open) each time it is clicked or activated with Enter or Space, in every mode. Pair it with `open` to let the button drive a controlled section.
